im the tiny rat that makes none of da rules -------------------------------------- (short serious review below) Very solid game, amazing art direction, it feels great to play (at least using KB+M which is what I'm using). Basic game feels a bit like gungeon. VERY cryptic. A lot of negative reviews are about this, but I think it's part of the charm and appeal of the game. Once you get used to it's language, it's easier to understand what the game is telling you. Still, you either like it or hate it. Stock-full of secrets and collectibles, many of them are HARD. Runs on their own can feel rather basic, but the secrets make up for it. The amount of morsels there are is rather low, though, despite being the main focus of the game. I hope to see future updates adding more of them. Passive items you find on runs aren't catalogued (unless it's unlocked through a secret i've yet to find) so it feels like it's missing one layer of completionism other roguelites tend to have. One or two little bugs Also, my first win was really weird because the final boss just turned into an intert cube of tofu lol
I have no idea whats going on and I absolutely love it
虽然官方中文有些指示依然有些让人摸不着头脑，但总体上依然是一款惊喜频出的小而美作品呢，boss不难，反而探图常有惊吓，价格略略贵，可以的话和等打折也没啥
i'm straight up morbing my morsels

Great art, cute mouse squeaks, lots of fun character designs, but gameplay is just too chaotic. The core design mantra seems to be "throw everything at the player and tell them nothing". Which, that can be fine, but the visual language of what hurts you vs helps you, with flashes or colors or sounds, needs to exist, and be consistent. There is no compendium, that I could find, to give you at least some info about the items you've already found. Also, be aware, it does the Binding of Isaac thing where it locks aiming to 8 directions. I didn't feel like I was playing it, so much as just pushing my creatures through each stage. I finished hard cheese mode in an hour, not because I'm good, or was able to strategize, or unlocked some progression that allowed me to grow, but because of some broken item that basically made me invulnerable. I have zero desire to move onto nightmare difficulty, if it's just more of this.

This trend of making games with no tutorial or explanation for anything just doesn't work for me. I waited a long time to be this frustrated and confused? Feels bad. Maybe the reviewer who said he would pay $80 for this (???) can write up a guide for the rest of us.

There seems to be something here but its so obtuse that i never really feel like anything i get actually makes a difference. The levels are not interesting to explore, and the extra rooms just dont add much, The mini games are okay but just feel like a random internet flash game for a bit of variety. The visuals are unique but nothing really stands out to me as "wow look at that".

一周目2小时打赢了一局完整的标准模式来写点东西，我很喜欢辐射谷物语，，这个游戏到处都有辐射谷的影子，于是发售就狠狠购入了，游戏的可玩性还是很高的，手感的话玩过以撒可能会更容易适应移动射击的操作模式，弹幕类型则是玩过辐射谷物语的玩家更好上手，后期真的密集，又有滞留又有漂浮，但有输出就不是问题对吧，，顺带一提游戏大部分怪物没有接触伤害，很舒适。 游戏里有种类还算比较多的糜兽可以玩，每个糜兽的攻击方式都不太一样，用同一个糜兽战斗久了还能进化，再然后我就不剧透了（？）轮椅糜兽不少，萌新玩家应该也能有较好的体验，流程长度的话看成就还有不少的隐藏区域没有去过，还有一些有意思的小细节，比如雨水天气可以给未成熟的雏菊浇水，还有我不知道干嘛使的地上印着数字的砖块，隐藏房间里的猫王干嘛使的，，需要摸索的地方挺多，娱乐开一把也很有意思 就这样，希望游戏和辐射谷一样能长久更新，，接着摸索去了XD 不要在读取地图的时候暂停，很容易卡死无法退出暂停界面，， 虫神的M挑战房疑似有问题，，没有延时的方法只能等死。 同一个奖励物品（如钱袋，猴子）无法生效两次，如果关卡里刷了俩也没必要都拿走 井字激光阵有概率秒杀（类似蛇咬） [spoiler] [u]切换难度疑似会清空真结局的卡牌碎片 [/u] [/spoiler] 二编有剧透相关： [spoiler]达成了全部糜兽的成就，目前来看幽灵糜兽和青蛙糜兽是隐藏的，无法通过卡牌获取，幽灵我是真不知道怎么获得的，也没使用过，但图鉴解锁了，【续：幽灵糜兽通过获得过时磁带后死亡获得，磁带会在商人处随机刷新】青蛙则是精灵天气事件被精灵施法就可以变，青蛙强度很高，但缺点是无法获得战利品，青蛙还可以在沼泽关卡打开隐藏房间，能拿到一把钥匙，但钥匙在哪用我就还没找到（这把钥匙似乎还能把你的糜兽全部变成青蛙）【续：钥匙在荒林关卡能找到一个圆环形状的门使用】 在天空章节可以用苍蝇逃课，不然困难难度打起来真坐牢，，用苍蝇能看到左上角的区域有无法抵达的区域，不知道是不是隐藏区域。 每只糜兽的M挑战房都是独特的关卡，打满能拿到对应的小雕像放在房间里 初始鼠鼠拿卡的房间那只写实浣熊有成就。 第二章垃圾岛刷新藏宝图，宝藏位置则在荒林刷新 在天空章节里梯子有概率【续：实际上是必刷】刷出一只月亮猫，打跑能开月球隐藏，月亮猫出现条件未知，不过感觉和随机刷新的巨大月亮脸有关系？月球上有一块碎片， [strike]需要用到泡泡兽（老实说更像粉色大便） [/strike]打出暴击伤害就行，别像我一样打一分钟都没触发还以为要特定糜兽。 大概是大更新前最后一次编辑评测，指南里已经有全成就指南大纲了，说点自己的想法 关于奶酪梦：在第一章第二章和第四章随机会刷三种奶酪，一个章节只会出现一种奶酪（至少我刷了十几把没出现过一章节出俩奶酪的时候） [h3]黄色奶酪 [/h3]最显眼，一进图就能听到它的哼哼声，在它逃跑前打掉就行。 [h3]绿色奶酪 [/h3]在奶酪喷泉里，建议是当前章节没出奶酪的时候把见过的池子全灌满，最头疼的是 [h3]紫色奶酪 [/h3]，每个章节里随机一个关卡会刷新一扇隐藏标记门，一扇粉色的M型标记房间（和挑战M房不同）无法直接进入，需要爆炸物才能炸开，进入能拿到隐藏道具，如果当前章节已经出过奶酪了会生成被动道具，这个隐藏房间是每章节固定刷的，但一章节只会在多个关卡里挑一关刷新，所以找起来很费眼睛。三个奶酪齐了以后会合成幽灵，在第五章天界里随机一关幽灵会睁眼，带着幽灵四处探图，此时的幽灵半径里能照亮出一条奶酪颜色的隐藏路径，跟着走就能进奶酪梦 关于小指头：月球上的小指头藏在陨石堆里，是个很显眼的问号，需要爆炸物才能打碎陨石，虽然场地里有一些爆炸草，但很容易被自己的随从误杀，建议带榴弹猪（这人老在起奇怪的外号） [h3] 调皮的[/h3] 这个要求真的挺苛刻的，我不知道评测作者那种方法是不是第二种可能性，我只说我自己参考别人总结的方法，它藏在第一章里，你需要一盘过时磁带变成幽灵，然后在第一章里仅有的三关里刷出雨天，接著在终点梯子附近看看有没有猫商人，老实说我觉得商人可能并不一定是必要的，接著用幽灵在地图边缘溜边，就能找到一个藏得很深的小指头，，总之 [h3] 推荐在第一章刷出幽灵后在雨天天气溜边寻找[/h3]幽灵可以在商人买，带眼睛会射子弹的电视也会固定掉. 我还有很多成就没有刷，也还有很多东西意义不明，比如第四章的高尔夫球洞干嘛的，石头围一圈的池塘又是干嘛的，到处贴满通缉海报的猫王真的没用吗，，这些都还没弄明白，，，以后再考虑吧。[/spoiler]

I really wanted to like this game because WOW the art is pretty, like, I will not say anything against it, the visual and audio experience are top-notch The issue is that the rest of the game simply doesn't feel good. The shooting is locked to eight directions, making aiming a bit of a slog especially on controller (the recommended experience) and overall lacks weight. While it is interesting that morsels have different moves, the relatively low amount of them and the noticeable balance difference between them can lead to just not much experimentation. Overall, the gameplay itself doesn't feel too satisfying, either, frankly. The fact that the game is greedy with its information would be fine if there were some ways to find things out, however, there just doesn't seem to be, beyond random tutorial boxes every so often. I am not against hidden mechanics at all, but I do feel as though the game hides its hand a bit too much. And unlike spelunky, it doesn't feel as though there is much problem solving between runs as much, or at least I did not feel encouraged to. Again, I'm very sad to give this a negative review, but its visual presentation doesn't make up for the rest.

At first glance, Morsels feels like chaos in motion. Most players — myself included — open the game thinking it’s too confusing, too messy, almost intentionally unclear. But that’s exactly where its magic sneaks in. Once you settle into its rhythm, Morsels delivers something rare: the feeling of playing games as a kid, when you didn’t fully understand the rules but you kept exploring anyway. You try, you fail, you poke at its weird corners, and somehow the confusion becomes part of the fun. It’s a messy little world, but it captures that pure childhood sensation of curiosity — where every attempt feels like discovery, not frustration. Morsels doesn’t explain itself, and in a strange way, that’s what makes it so charming.

The final boss was turned into a block of tofu by an ability with no description. What the ♥♥♥♥ man. Okay, okay, in all seriousness... This game is a gorgeous artistic experience, but the gameplay is just... Bad. There are like, 11 morsels, and while they're all cute and unique and stuff, you HAVE to cycle through them, so it never feels like your build's amounting to anything. The events between levels are horribly bare-bones... And nothing gets explained, which wouldn't be a problem for me usually! Morsels DOES let you root around in its weird lil world and figure everything out... But the reward for figuring things out isn't really there. And again, I won my first run because the final boss was randomly replaced by a block of tofu. The art is gorgeous and I love Toby Dixon... but the game just isn't fun to play, which SUCKS, because I REALLY wanna like this game! I'm a massive fan of the works of Toby Dixon, and Morsels is indeed just as pretty and stylish as I wanted it to be... but there's sadly very little substance behind the style.

I have been waiting for this game for about 6 months now, I and I'm very underwhelmed by the final product. The sound design and art style is a 10/10 but the gameplay is lacking. The items items don't tell you anything and there are barely any morsels to choose from. The difficulty of the game isn't even hard and I beat the game one my very first run and for a roguelike, that is crazy. SO sad that I waited so long for this game to be sub-par :(

The art style is quite fun, but enemies, the protagonist, attacks, backgrounds, and clutter are all way too similar. Sometimes I can’t even tell where I am, turning what should be a charming art style into a mess. The difficulty comes from the protagonist’s abysmally low stats. Not sure if it’s due to Chinese translation issues, but many things are completely incomprehensible. Why did a ghost cat suddenly start following me around nonstop with no way to get rid of it? A bunch of speed boost items—once you reach heaven, you fall off the map with just one move. Surely the developer doesn’t think that’s entertaining? When I got to the moon, entered a sewer teleport, and died before I even saw where my character was. I had a bunch of flowers above my head, full health, and no snakes spawned. With that setup, I have no clue what killed me. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 画面风格很有趣，但是怪物、主角、攻击、背景、杂物，这些东西太过于相同，有时候分不清我在哪儿，于是乎本来很有趣的画面风格就变成一坨垃圾。 难度在于主角的性能太低。 不知道是不是因为中文翻译的问题，很多东西压根不知道是干嘛的，怎么突然就有个幽灵猫全程跟着我还无法驱散。 一堆加速道具到天界动一下就掉出地图，作者该不会觉得很有趣吧。 到月球进了个下水道传送后我还没看到我人在哪儿我就死了。我头上一堆花，血量满的，蛇也没出来，就这配置连被啥干掉的都不知道。

I'm not really sure why we had to wait for this game to come out after the demo. There really isn't much to this game. It's like a game you rent at Blockbuster or the grocery store and beat it in one night and then never play it again. The game is pretty cool, but gets old fast and nothing makes sense. I don't know or care what any of the Morbs do, all you really need to worry about is getting the right guys, mutating them, and saving the best ones for the bosses. Or you just get that special mode from the Hacker and it doesn't matter what you do, the short game is beat. The levels have no goals or purpose, you can finish every level without even fighting anyone, or collecting anything?! There are so many mysterious things about the game, and after beating it on multiple difficulty settings, one-shoting bosses with the most powerful mutated morsel and pebbling through each level in matters of seconds, nothing has really changed, I only have 3 achievements, and there is no clues at all about what else there is to the game. I've already played this game enough times over and over again, I really don't want to play it anymore to see if their might be some other tiny thing to unlock. Definitely just play the demo, you're not missing much. If you are looking for an awesome, masterfully made, old school style game that has plenty of silly weirdness, I would highly recommend trying Garbanzo Quest that came out last year if you haven't already, I believe that game is tippity top-notch, it got my vote for game of the year last year and I would vote for it again this year. Peace :)

I like learning this as much as the next person, but in most rogues, once you learn something, it's stored in your guidebook/etc. Not here. You get no idea on what you're doing and have to rely entirely on your memory for, well, everything. And the very very very basics of the game aren't even explained to you. The gameplay itself is fun, but figuring out the basic mechanics of the game is not.

【21世纪水压套圈游戏机】——命名为《超超超级嘉年华3000》，其实数不清的放课后小摊贩玩完就丢小玩具's用电线捆成一捆，不过本以为会像前作让眼睛没法玩的饱和度一样原地爆炸...但这一‘特质’却与【核类】童年记忆的元素还有低质量模糊滤镜完美匹配而安定下来，再加上遥远但又似录音室回音的配乐音效，臭臭丑丑的但又有点 jellycat梦幻治愈的糜兽设计，营造了种浓郁的——夏日午夜晚间市集曲终人散，但留下卡通角色海报彩纸，零星未灭的灯火光晕和星光形成了五彩斑斓的黑，介于最后一缕烟火气和孤独之间的中间状态，使家里蹲人也能安心地嘴角微微泛起甜腻味道。 游戏营造的玩法也是如此——快节奏以命换命的环境，完全不同手感细腻的14个糜兽玩法（比如湘西赶尸菇，越吃越长变异贪食蛇，蓄力棒球小子，呕吐喷射苍蝇，冲刺无敌石头便便，尾气打人地刺虫，低血量一口吞诅咒青蛙）和各式花样小游戏不重样的隐藏房间轮番轰炸（猪猪巴士的过马路游戏让我印象深刻，与被车撞后看见白洞的童年记忆相耦合），道具没有任何文字提示的肉鸽，【真的有种童年的投币街机（游戏内的快速开始键也映衬了这一点）的快乐！！】眼花缭乱玩不明白在注意力情绪被调动到高处时就用完了零花钱的几个币，CRT显示器一角来历不明的贴纸告诉你这五彩斑斓并不属于你，十分到位的...混乱&疏远&无能的怪核情绪体验。 ！！！！！！！但是！！！！！！！如果您比起超级绚烂的怪核美学氛围更关心正常肉鸽游戏的那种构筑深度和重玩的变化的话，目前游戏在这个方向基本没有（个人觉得将来也挺难做到）： 每个糜兽的构筑深度只有：一次升级+一个专属神器，其他都是换谁都可以的通用特效（小鸟，菊花，闪烁）和属性提升，推高后有变化但不会形成分支....可能制作者想让3个糜兽位的切换来起到每局变化的效果，但目前看来也是各打各的（如果要有构筑机制那十多种的糜兽有自己专属的成长路线，那必须再添加海量的新内容...短期不大可能做到） 另外层底的增益？选择也是如此，虽然选择都和童年成长高度相关的很有趣契合主题（比如时间就是金钱&金钱就是生命，随着移动和停止来控制时间流速，看电视的那层什么也不会发生笑死XD,而且用下来都挺负面的，也算是某种形式的成长痛拉hh）但也真的很孤立于构筑，导致4,5h的快乐散场后只能玩完就丢（虽然个人觉得很值得，就像嘉年华的门票票根），很难有重玩欲望...
Ass
手感一流特效和打击感非常有特色，糜兽到3级就会被养死看似是很奇怪的设定，但是死去的糜兽会留下一个升级道具让之后的糜兽能在开大时出发死去糜兽的技能特效（比如泡泡糖兽留下的道具会让以后所有糜兽开大都能释放护盾），某种程度上要考验玩家的运营和技术（要是只剩下一个即将老死的糜兽那就必输无疑了）

说实话我还蛮喜欢这个游戏的画风的，实际上游戏玩法中规中矩，明显的boss弱于地图，还有糜兽的强度完全不对等，叶子苍蝇大招超模，炸弹和石头勉强算对策卡，植物叠得太慢，还气短，烟头简直废，如果不考虑挑战玩法的话我见到都不会拿。当然，如果只是平衡问题我不至于打差评，差评的实际原因是它bug很难受。这个游戏没有实时存档功能，又偶尔闪退，虽然只是偶尔，但它在我打超大杯平克闪退了···白打两百多局···他的bug还包括打死楼梯守护不掉楼梯，还有个更恶劣的，打怪不掉血，伤害是显示的，怪吃了我二级叶子三个大就是不死，最后被蛇怪机制杀了···这种现象出现了4次，体验及其不好（虽然我还是喜欢这款游戏，谁叫我喜欢“没事找虐”呢）
i like the wierd little guys
只能说玩过工作室之前的作品辐射谷我对这作抱有了太高的期望，结果是令我很失望的，无论是游戏性还玩法深度上都大不如前作，虽然是肉鸽但是根本没啥构筑性可言，基本上只要拿到好用的卡，其他附加的就只是锦上添花了，除了了那个受伤瞬移是真的一坨屎，妥妥的负加强，千万别选 但是美术确实很好，有个性又鲜活，肯定是比辐射谷好多了的 要说这作最大的意义大概就就是唤醒了我回去玩辐射谷的心情，不说了辐射谷启动！

Can't deny it looks and sounds great. Great vibes, but gameplay is just a morsel lol. Powerups and items feel sparse and offered little (often, no) explanation of their effects. Binding of Isaac did this, but there, the effects were much more apparent with gameplay. Here, I still have little idea what's going on 3 hours in. I don't like traversing between the levels as it's punishing for no fault of my own. There are between level events, many of them require you to lose one of your morsels (you can switch between 3 different "morsels" that change your attacks). Definitely room for improvement in the future, I'm really rooting for them.

Game is confusing, punishes you for performing too well, punishments are needlessly punishing, and there doesn't seem to be any intention of addressing any of it. The game throws a billion different icons in your face, and if you wish to have a decent run, you are expected decipher what it means amidst several other icons you don't know what they do, and then remember it, even though I love discovery in video games, I hate having to replace my childhood memories with the technical descriptions of items to not pick up. I thought this thing of having to remember what literally everything does was the biggest flaw of TBOI. To add to this, you are expected to rush to the end of each level, with a slow unkillable threat if you don't, akin to Spelunky, but it's counter-intuitive due to some parts of levels being way too difficult, if not impossible, to clear from having projectile spamming enemies intentionally stuck inside walls, or constant threats on levels that are seemingly cursed for some unexplained reason. As for the creature collecting the game advertises, you play as these creatures, and you lose if they all die, OR you can evolve your creature by earning xp, once to make it stronger, twice to transform it to an orbiting sprite that is way weaker, but lasts until the end of a run. Problem is, if you earn too much xp without finding a new creature with your limited slots and availability for each level, before transforming all your creatures and killing your run (literally) from success. This essentially bottlenecks how strong you are allowed to become from your educated decisions, as you have to ignore strong item combos, as to not suffer from this. On the topic of the game's advertising, the roguelite elements to the game are, or is rather, cause it only really has a single roguelite element, being a boring level system that progresses based on your runs' success that unlocks buffs that are randomly assigned to the creatures you find that may or may not be nerfs, rather than buffs, in practice. The game does have one other roguelite feature; a creature in a hidden corridor within the starting place, which leaves you with vague very clues of where and how to find its children, which I have yet to complete. While I love the art of the game, and gameplay generally being smooth, it has these major flaws that I doubt will ever be addressed, as all I can find of the team on social media and their website has lied dormant since release, and the last activity I could find from them at all, is the last minor patch to the game from mid February. This is really unfortunate, as the game Atomicrops with the same artist, who lead the production of this game, is my favorite roguelite.

Morsels is a creature-collecting action roguelite developed by Furcula and published by Annapurna Interactive that combines fast-paced combat, unusual world design, and monster-based gameplay into an experience built around experimentation and replayability. Rather than following the traditional structure of creature collection games focused on exploration and turn-based systems, Morsels takes a far stranger direction. It mixes frantic action with roguelite progression while building an identity driven by surreal ideas, unpredictable encounters, and constant adaptation. The game introduces players to an unusual protagonist: a small mouse struggling to survive in a harsh underground environment. That relatively simple beginning quickly becomes far stranger after encountering a mysterious force that grants transformative powers. What starts as an ordinary survival story develops into something far more bizarre, opening the door to strange creatures, dangerous enemies, and a larger conflict hidden beneath the surface. The setting embraces absurdity confidently while maintaining enough structure to keep players invested in discovering what comes next. One of the game's strongest features revolves around creature management. Instead of controlling a single character permanently, players gather powerful creatures called Morsels and actively switch between them during combat encounters. Every creature brings different strengths, abilities, and utility options that influence survival strategies. Some focus heavily on direct offense while others provide mobility advantages or defensive support. Success depends heavily on understanding when to rotate between creatures rather than relying entirely on a single approach. Combat moves quickly and rewards active playstyles. Enemy encounters frequently place pressure on positioning and reaction speed, forcing players to stay mobile while adapting to changing situations. Dodging attacks, understanding enemy patterns, and using creature abilities effectively become critical components of survival. The faster pacing helps maintain excitement while supporting the game's chaotic identity. The creature systems create impressive strategic depth beneath the colorful presentation. Different combinations create opportunities for experimentation, encouraging players to discover interactions between creatures and upgrades rather than following rigid progression paths. Strong combinations feel satisfying because they emerge naturally through experimentation rather than scripted progression systems. Roguelite mechanics strengthen long-term engagement significantly. Individual runs evolve differently depending on discovered upgrades, creature availability, and progression choices made throughout each attempt. Randomization introduces variety while preserving enough structure to reward mastery over time. Failure rarely feels wasted because repeated attempts gradually improve understanding while opening stronger possibilities for future runs. Replay value becomes one of Morsels' biggest strengths because no two attempts unfold exactly the same way. Different creature combinations, progression paths, and unexpected discoveries create variety naturally. The game consistently encourages experimentation rather than optimization alone, helping longer play sessions remain engaging. Presentation also contributes heavily to the overall experience. The visual style embraces strange creature designs, exaggerated animation, and environments filled with personality. Rather than aiming for realism, Morsels builds atmosphere through distinctive artistic choices that reinforce its unusual world. The visual identity feels memorable because it commits fully to its surreal ideas. Audio design strengthens that identity further. Music supports combat pacing effectively while quieter moments allow environmental atmosphere and strange worldbuilding details to stand out. Sound design contributes heavily to maintaining energy during combat-heavy moments while preserving the game's distinctive personality. The roguelite structure naturally creates a learning curve that may initially challenge some players. Certain systems require experimentation before their full potential becomes clear. Players unfamiliar with progression-heavy roguelites may occasionally feel overwhelmed by available mechanics during early attempts. However, repeated play gradually reveals stronger understanding while reinforcing long-term satisfaction. Balance between randomness and player agency works especially well. Randomized progression creates unpredictability, but player decisions consistently influence outcomes enough to prevent success from feeling purely dependent on luck. Strategic planning and mechanical execution remain equally valuable throughout progression. What ultimately makes Morsels stand out is how confidently it embraces unusual ideas without sacrificing mechanical depth. The creature systems remain meaningful. Combat remains consistently engaging. Roguelite progression strengthens replayability without overwhelming experimentation. The game succeeds because it avoids becoming predictable. Strange ideas continue appearing throughout progression while core mechanics remain strong enough to support repeated play. The combination creates an experience that feels inventive while remaining mechanically rewarding. Morsels delivers rewarding combat systems, creative creature mechanics, memorable presentation, and excellent replay value while successfully blending roguelite structure with fast-paced action and unusual world design. Rating: 7/10

[h1] What matters most in reviews is sincerity and consistency. [/h1] Let me tell you, it's so hard for me to write a negative review for any game [spoiler](no matter how much I hate it)[/spoiler] as I almost always understand and moreover [u]believe that any game can be enjoyed by specific people and in specific contexts[/u]. Therefore, any negative review can push the game down and hurt its talented and artful developers. But as a curator, if I write [b]ONLY[/b] positive reviews, [b]I'll have no value whatsoever as a reviewer[/b], because people couldn't see what drives me as a human being and would't relate to me. Therefore, after much thought, I decided to face my moral struggle and write [i]my first negative review.[/i] Morsels is surely a game? It comes from the great creators of atomicrops, which I enjoy so much. I was hyped for this game and bought it almost immediately. Unfortunately, [u]it didn't live up to the hype, and it tells a lot, as I had almost no expectations[/u]. After only an hour of playing, I really felt demotivated to seek anything else in the game, as [b]the game loop doesn't feel satisfying at all for me[/b]. I like the classic art style; the sound design is great, and it could be debated that the game, in all its strengths and flaws, is unique. But [b]it just doesn't click[/b]. I really can't explain it fully. It feels like the game doesn't have "the sauce". It's just... kind of bland even with so many crazy choices. As always I advise to test this game out for yourself, but for me it's a miss. P.S - If you want to read more of my reviews [spoiler]https://store.steampowered.com/curator/46139049/ [/spoiler]

Great action, great environment art, great music, great character design, etc. Fun, clunky, and weird. This game is like a creature you found living under a rock in the forest. A creature that would have always existed there with or without anyone's knowledge. Doing its own thing. Eating whatever it eats. It has its own logic and culture that you can try to understand if you choose. If you're into that kind of experience, I would say buy this game. It's a rare treat in this climate of handholding media. I'm still figuring out the combat's rhythm, but that has been part of the fun too. Lastly: the music is GREAT. In a fuzzy, moldy, funky way. I played the demo for hours and have listened to the soundtrack on and off while driving ever since. I'm glad I finally purchased this beautiful, hairy booger. My sweet, sweet booger.
